summary: Protected PR #1003 delivers this source-only witness; runtime qualification remains separate from this source finding. The test launches the actual pinned Python callback owner and holds its controlled typed-slot backend inside ordinal-six readback while the managed transport retains actual WriteAsync request aliases and independent endpoint copies. One fresh test nonce, canonical binding digest, digest of the thirteen requests actually read by Python, and both process IDs correlate the observations. Release requires exactly nonce/binding/request/ordinal/stage; before/after Python samples must retain identical object identities and lengths. The managed source assertions count thirteen distinct original request arrays plus thirteen independent endpoint copies (25,738 scoped logical bytes); the pinned Python observer counts sixteen distinct objects (11,660 scoped logical bytes). These counts exclude other objects, allocator capacity, task/channel storage and uncertain paths and do not establish a complete simultaneous physical population, release or a 65,536-byte fit. The test subsequently asserts six exact typed slots, three ACKs, terminal response confirmation and settled retained tasks, while preserving first failure and joining cleanup. Terminal evidence explicitly denies input EOF/trailing-input checks and operational-receipt status. The producer pin selects FS-GG/.github revision d84e66bc2eafc44b6f53e7ef0b20ed6f1477cc95, and the owner hashes the selected lifetime observer/profile before loading. This source witness does not establish native authentication, host custody, replay authority, original-operation effects or installed adoption.
title: Managed/Python source witness holds ordinal-six readback in one correlated execution
